paragraphs: The water cycle is how water moves around the Earth. Water from oceans, rivers, and lakes goes up into the sky. This process is called evaporation.
When water goes up, it changes into tiny drops called water vapor. These drops come together to make clouds. This is called condensation.
When the clouds get heavy, water falls back down as rain or snow. This is called precipitation. Then the water goes back to the oceans and the cycle starts again. The water cycle never stops.
Water can also collect underground. This is called groundwater. People pump groundwater up through wells to use for drinking and farming.
The water cycle is important for all living things. Without it, there would be no rain and no fresh water. The same water has been moving around the Earth for millions of years.

paragraphs: The solar system is made up of the Sun and eight planets. The Sun is a big star at the center. All the planets go around the Sun in paths called orbits.
The four planets closest to the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars. They are made of rock and have hard surfaces. We call them the inner planets.
The four planets far away are Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. They are very big and made of gas. We call them the outer planets.
Earth is the only planet where we know there is life. It has water, air, and the right temperature. Mars is very cold, but scientists are studying it to see if life was there long ago.
The Sun gives us light and heat. Without the Sun, Earth would be very cold and dark. All life on Earth needs the Sun to live and grow.

paragraphs: Plants are living things that grow all around us. They need four important things to grow: water, sunlight, air, and soil. Without these things, plants cannot live.
Most plants start as tiny seeds. A seed has a small plant inside it. When the seed gets enough water and warmth, it begins to grow. First, a small root goes down into the soil.
Then a green shoot pushes up through the soil to find sunlight. The shoot grows taller and grows leaves. The leaves catch sunlight and use it to make food for the plant.
Roots take in water and minerals from the soil. They also hold the plant in the ground so it does not fall over. A healthy plant grows strong and makes new seeds.
Some plants grow flowers, and flowers make seeds. When the seeds fall on the ground, new plants can grow. This is how plants make more plants and keep living.

paragraphs: A volcano is a mountain with an opening at the top. Deep inside the Earth, it is very hot. Rocks there melt and become a thick liquid called magma.
When the magma gets too hot, it pushes up and comes out through the opening. When it reaches the surface, we call it lava. Lava flows down the sides of the mountain.
Volcanoes can be dangerous, but they also help the Earth. The ash from volcanoes makes soil very good for growing plants. Some volcanoes are active, and others are sleeping.
Scientists called volcanologists study volcanoes. They watch for signs that a volcano might erupt. This helps keep people who live near volcanoes safe.
There are volcanoes under the ocean too. When they erupt, they can make new islands. Some islands in the world were made by volcanoes under the sea.

paragraphs: A food chain shows how energy moves from one living thing to another. It always starts with a plant. Plants make their own food using sunlight, so they are called producers.
Animals that eat plants are called herbivores. They are the second step in the food chain. Animals that eat other animals are called carnivores. They are the third step.
Some animals eat both plants and animals. We call them omnivores. At the top of the food chain are the strongest animals. If one animal disappears, the whole chain can break.
A food web is many food chains connected together. Most animals eat more than one kind of food. Food webs show how all the living things in a place are connected.
People are part of food chains too. We eat plants and animals. It is important to protect all parts of the food chain so that nature stays in balance.

readings.title: The Human Heart

paragraphs: The heart is a muscle inside your chest. It is about the size of your fist. The heart pumps blood to every part of your body. It works all day and all night without stopping.
Your heart has four rooms inside it. Blood comes in through two rooms and goes out through the other two. The blood carries oxygen from the air you breathe to all your body.
When you run or exercise, your heart beats faster. This is because your muscles need more oxygen. You can feel your heart beat by putting your hand on your chest. A healthy heart keeps you strong.
Doctors can listen to your heart with a tool called a stethoscope. It makes the sound of your heartbeat louder. A normal heart beats about 70 to 80 times per minute when you rest.
To keep your heart healthy, you should eat good food and exercise every day. Foods like fruits and vegetables are good for your heart. Smoking and too much junk food can hurt your heart.

readings.title: Clouds and Weather
paragraphs: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water and ice. They float in the sky because the drops are very small and light. There are many different kinds of clouds in the sky.
Cumulus clouds look like big white cotton balls. They usually mean fair weather. Stratus clouds are flat and gray. They often bring rain or light snow.
Cirrus clouds are thin and look like feathers high up in the sky. They tell us that a change in weather is coming. Cumulonimbus clouds are very tall and can bring storms.
Weather changes because the Sun heats the Earth in different ways. Warm air goes up and cold air comes down. This movement of air makes wind, rain, and all our weather.
Meteorologists are scientists who study the weather. They use tools to measure temperature, wind, and rain. They can tell us if it will be sunny or rainy tomorrow.

readings.title: The Ocean
paragraphs: The ocean covers most of the Earth's surface. It has salt water and is home to millions of animals. Fish, whales, and sharks live in the ocean. There are also tiny plants called plankton.
The ocean is very deep. In some places, it is deeper than the tallest mountains on land. Sunlight only reaches the top part. Down in the deep, it is very dark and cold.
Waves are made when the wind blows across the water. The ocean also has currents, which are like rivers moving inside the sea. The ocean gives us food and helps control the climate.
The ocean has five main parts: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic oceans. The Pacific is the biggest. It covers more area than all the land on Earth put together.
The ocean is very important for our planet. It gives us oxygen, food, and helps keep the Earth warm enough for life. We must protect the ocean from pollution.

readings.title: Photosynthesis
paragraphs: Photosynthesis is the way plants make their own food. The word means making food with light. Plants use sunlight, water, and a gas called carbon dioxide to make sugar.
This process happens in the leaves of the plant. Leaves are green because they have a substance called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll catches the sunlight that the plant needs.
When plants make sugar, they also make oxygen. This oxygen goes into the air. Animals and people need oxygen to breathe. So plants are very important for all life on Earth.
Plants do not photosynthesize at night because there is no sunlight. At night, plants rest and use the sugar they made during the day. This is similar to how animals rest after eating.
Without photosynthesis, there would be no food for any living thing. Plants are the start of every food chain. That is why protecting plants and forests is so important.

readings.title: Animal Adaptations
paragraphs: Animals have special features that help them survive in their homes. These features are called adaptations. For example, polar bears have thick fur to stay warm in the cold snow.
Some animals use camouflage to hide from other animals. A chameleon can change its color to match the place around it. This makes it very hard to see.
Other animals have adaptations for finding food. A giraffe has a very long neck to eat leaves from tall trees. A dolphin uses sound to find fish in the dark ocean.
Some animals can even change how their body works. A frog can sleep all winter long to survive the cold. Adaptations help animals live in many different places around the world.
Plants have adaptations too. Cactus plants store water in their thick stems to survive in dry deserts. Some plants in cold places grow close to the ground to stay warm.
